description:
We’re building a Marswalk planner for astronauts. Using NASA terrain, thermal and weather data from Jezero Crater, it plans safe EVA routes for a crew and their support rover, balancing slope, hazards, suit thermal limits, solar power and radiation. Looking for teammates in Python, GIS, data analysis or web development who want to build something real with NASA data.

Fast learners are welcome!
summary: Marswalk Navigators is an interactive Mars map that plans safe routes for an astronaut on foot and a support rover across the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp, where Curiosity explored in 2025. We stacked real NASA data into one map: HiRISE elevation and imagery, THEMIS thermal infrared, Curiosity’s traverse and photos, RAD radiation and REMS weather. You click a start and an end, and the planner finds a route that avoids slopes and rough ground each traveller can’t handle. Then it works out the walk’s time, energy, oxygen, radiation dose and suit cooling load. Along the way it suggests science stops picked from real Curiosity targets, and it estimates the wheel loads the terrain puts on the rover. Future crews will need to know where to walk, what it costs them and what the ground will do to their hardware before they step outside, and this tool answers all three on one screen.
details:
What it does: a web map of a 4 by 6 km area of Mount Sharp in Gale crater. Layers show Curiosity’s path, a go/caution/no-go hazard map from slope and roughness, THEMIS night infrared (firm rock vs loose sand) and RAD dose. The A* pathfinding algorithm plans separate astronaut and rover routes on a 20 m terrain grid, each with its own slope limit (25° on foot, 20° for the rover).
Budgets: for each route it gives walking and driving time, metabolic energy, oxygen use, rover energy and solar power, radiation dose from RAD, and suit cooling load from REMS ground and air temperatures.
Science and engineering: 8 science stops based on real Curiosity targets, each with rover photos, plus wheel load cases from the steepest and roughest ground for structural analysis.
Benefits and impact: mission planners and crews can compare routes by safety, cost and science value before an EVA.
Tools: Python (NumPy, rasterio, FastAPI), JavaScript, Leaflet, HTML/CSS, hosted on Vercel, with the code on GitHub.
What makes it creative: it links terrain, the human body and rover hardware in one planner.
What we considered: real data only, with every assumption written down in the code and README.
dataRefs: THEMIS day and night infrared (Mars Odyssey)
